title: Professional Project Proposal Template
description: Free professional project proposal template for freelancers, agencies, consultants, and service providers. Copy, customize, and download instantly.
intro: A professional project proposal helps freelancers, consultants, agencies, and service providers present a clear solution, define deliverables, establish timelines, and secure client approval before work begins. whenToUse: Use this template when pitching services, consulting work, creative projects, marketing campaigns, software development, operational improvements, or client engagements. It is commonly used for freelance work, agency retainers, B2B service proposals, and professional project bids.

faqs.question: What is a project proposal?
faqs.answer: A project proposal is a structured document that outlines a solution, project scope, timeline, pricing, and terms in order to secure client or stakeholder approval.

faqs.question: Why should project proposals include out-of-scope items?
faqs.answer: Clearly defining out-of-scope work helps prevent misunderstandings, unexpected revisions, and scope creep during the project.

faqs.question: Should pricing be itemized in a proposal?
faqs.answer: Yes, transparent pricing tables help clients understand exactly what services and deliverables are included.

faqs.question: Why are timelines and milestones important?
faqs.answer: Milestones help establish accountability, track progress, and set expectations for project delivery.

faqs.question: What should happen after a proposal is approved?
faqs.answer: After approval, both parties typically sign the proposal or move into a formal project agreement or contract.

faqs.question: What is an influencer media kit?
faqs.answer: An influencer media kit is a professional portfolio that presents audience demographics, engagement metrics, content examples, collaboration history, and partnership opportunities to brands.

faqs.question: How long should a media kit be?
faqs.answer: Most effective media kits are one to two pages long and focus on the most important information brands need to evaluate a partnership.

faqs.question: Should engagement rate be included?
faqs.answer: Yes. Engagement rate is often more important to brands than follower count because it demonstrates audience activity and trust.

faqs.question: Should rates be included in a media kit?
faqs.answer: Some creators include rates while others provide pricing upon request. Either approach can work depending on the creator's negotiation strategy.

faqs.question: How often should a media kit be updated?
faqs.answer: Media kits should be updated whenever significant audience growth occurs and at least once every quarter.

faqs.question: What analytics matter most to brands?
faqs.answer: Brands typically focus on engagement rate, audience demographics, reach, impressions, audience location, and previous campaign performance.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a Profit and Loss Statement and a Balance Sheet?
faqs.answer: A Profit and Loss Statement shows revenue, expenses, and profitability over a period of time, while a Balance Sheet shows assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific point in time.

faqs.question: How often should a P&L statement be prepared?
faqs.answer: Most businesses prepare P&L statements monthly, quarterly, and annually to monitor financial performance and support decision-making.

faqs.question: What is EBITDA?
faqs.answer: EBITDA stands for Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization. It measures core operating performance before financing and accounting adjustments.

faqs.question: What is gross profit?
faqs.answer: Gross profit is revenue minus Cost of Goods Sold (COGS). It measures how efficiently a business delivers its products or services.

faqs.question: Can freelancers and solopreneurs use a P&L statement?
faqs.answer: Yes. P&L statements are valuable for freelancers, consultants, creators, agencies, and businesses of any size.

faqs.question: What is a creator rate card?
faqs.answer: A creator rate card is a professional pricing document that lists a creator's services, deliverables, base rates, usage rights, add-ons, and package options for brand partnerships.

faqs.question: How is a rate card different from a media kit?

faqs.question: Should creators include usage rights on a rate card?

faqs.question: How should creators price sponsored posts?
faqs.answer: Creators often price sponsored posts using a combination of follower count, engagement rate, average views, content type, production time, niche value, and usage rights.

faqs.question: What are common creator rate card add-ons?
faqs.answer: Common add-ons include paid usage rights, whitelisting, exclusivity, raw footage, additional revisions, rush delivery, extra hooks, scriptwriting, and link-in-bio placement.

faqs.question: How often should a creator update their rate card?
faqs.answer: Most creators should update their rate card every three to six months or whenever their audience, engagement, niche demand, or portfolio quality significantly improves.

title: Standard Operating Procedure Template
description: Professional standard operating procedure template for businesses, teams, agencies, creators, operations managers, and growing organizations. Document repeatable workflows, assign responsibilities, define quality standards, and create clear step-by-step instructions for consistent results.
intro: A Standard Operating Procedure, or SOP, is a clear step-by-step document that explains how to complete a recurring task consistently. It helps businesses reduce errors, train new team members, preserve institutional knowledge, and make sure important work is completed the same way every time. This template can be used for operations, content creation, brand outreach, editing, approvals, customer service, administrative workflows, and internal business processes.
whenToUse: Use this template when documenting a repeatable process that needs consistency, training support, quality control, compliance, or team-wide clarity. It is especially useful when a workflow depends on one person's knowledge, produces inconsistent results, or needs to be delegated to employees, contractors, assistants, editors, marketers, or operations staff.

Department: [Department]

Prepared By: [Name]

[Describe the process]

- [Completion requirement 1]
- [Completion requirement 2]

[Name / Role]

Reviewer:
[Name / Role]
Responsible for reviewing work for accuracy and quality.

[Name / Role]
Responsible for final approval before completion or publication.

==================================================
5. REQUIRED INPUTS AND RESOURCES
==================================================

Tools Required:

- [Tool / Software]
- [Tool / Software]
- [Tool / Software]

Templates Required:

- [Template Name]
- [Template Name]

Access Required:

- [Login / System / Folder]
- [Shared Drive / CRM / CMS / Project Manager]

Materials Required:

- [Raw file]
- [Client brief]
- [Brand guide]
- [Source document]

Reference Documents:

- [Policy]
- [Checklist]
- [Style Guide]
- [Training Guide]

==================================================
6. PROCEDURE
==================================================

Step 1: Prepare the Workspace

1. Open [Tool / Platform].
2. Locate [Folder / Project / Account].
3. Confirm that all required inputs are available.
4. If any required input is missing, notify [Responsible Person] before continuing.

Step 2: Review the Request or Brief

1. Read the full request, brief, ticket, or assignment.
2. Confirm the objective, deadline, audience, and required output.
3. Check for special instructions, brand rules, compliance requirements, or client notes.
4. Add questions or blockers to [Communication Channel].

Step 3: Complete the Main Task

1. Follow the approved workflow for [Task Name].
2. Use the required template, checklist, or system.
3. Complete each required section carefully.
4. Save work in the correct file location.
5. Name files using the approved naming convention:

[YYYY-MM-DD_ProjectName_Deliverable_Version]

Step 4: Quality Check

1. Review the completed work against the Definition of Done.
2. Confirm that all required fields, steps, files, or deliverables are complete.
3. Check spelling, formatting, accuracy, links, dates, names, calculations, and attachments.
4. Confirm that the work follows brand, client, legal, privacy, or compliance requirements.

Step 5: Submit for Review

1. Change task status to [Ready for Review].
2. Assign the reviewer in [Project Management Tool].
3. Include a short summary of what was completed.
4. Attach or link all supporting files.

Step 6: Complete Revisions

1. Review all comments from the reviewer or approver.
2. Make required changes.
3. Reply to comments that require clarification.
4. Resubmit for review when revisions are complete.

Step 7: Final Approval

1. Confirm that the approver has reviewed the final version.
2. Obtain written approval through [Tool / Email / Checklist / Signature].
3. Change task status to [Approved] or [Complete].

Step 8: Archive and Record Completion

1. Save the final version in [Folder / System].
2. Update the tracking sheet, CRM, calendar, or project record.
3. Record completion date.
4. Note any issues, delays, or improvements for future updates.

==================================================

- Clear and easy to understand;
- Properly formatted;
- Saved in the correct location;
- Reviewed before submission;
- Approved before publication or delivery;
- Compliant with company policies and applicable requirements.

==================================================

Solution: Contact [Responsible Person] and pause the workflow until the missing information is provided.

Issue: Access to the required tool is unavailable.
Solution: Submit an access request to [Person / Department] and notify the process owner.

Issue: Reviewer does not respond by the deadline.
Solution: Send a follow-up message and escalate to [Manager / Approver] if no response is received within [Timeframe].

Issue: The task does not fit the standard process.
Solution: Document the exception and ask the process owner for guidance before proceeding.

==================================================
9. COMMON DECISION POINTS
==================================================

If the task is urgent:
Follow the rush workflow and notify [Approver].

If the task requires legal, compliance, or client approval:
Do not publish, send, or finalize until written approval is received.

If the task requires a new template:
Create a draft and submit it to the process owner for review.

If the task is blocked:
Update the task status to [Blocked] and document the reason.

==================================================

1. Complete the content brief.
2. Confirm target audience, keyword, goal, deadline, and call-to-action.
3. Draft the content in [Google Docs / CMS / Writing Tool].
4. Apply brand formatting and style guidelines.
5. Add images, captions, alt text, links, and metadata.
6. Run a self-review for clarity, accuracy, and completeness.
7. Submit the draft for editorial review.
8. Complete requested revisions.
9. Submit for final approval.
10. Move the asset to the publishing queue.

==================================================

1. Identify a qualified prospect.
2. Verify the contact name, company, website, and email address.
3. Research the brand's recent campaigns, products, and goals.
4. Personalize the outreach message.
5. Send the first-touch email.
6. Log the contact in [CRM / Spreadsheet / Airtable].

10. Move the opportunity to negotiation or closed status.

==================================================

1. Review the original brief.
2. Read the full draft before editing.
3. Check structure, logic, flow, and audience fit.
4. Edit for clarity, tone, grammar, punctuation, and formatting.
5. Verify claims, names, links, dates, and sources.
6. Leave specific comments where the creator must revise.
7. Mark the draft as [Ready for Approval] when complete.

==================================================
13. APPROVAL WORKFLOW EXAMPLE
==================================================

1. Reviewer submits the asset for approval.
2. Approver reviews the full asset, not only the changed sections.
3. Approver leaves clear comments or approves the asset.
4. Creator or editor completes any requested revisions.
5. Approver gives final written sign-off.
6. Asset moves to publishing, delivery, or archive.

14. DOCUMENT CONTROL
==================================================

[Shared Drive / Knowledge Base / Wiki / SOP Folder]

Naming Convention:
[SOP-ID_Process-Name_Version_Date]

Review Frequency:
[Every 6 Months / Annually / After Major Process Change]

[Name / Role]

15. VERSION HISTORY
==================================================

| Version | Date | Updated By | Changes Made |
|---------|------|------------|--------------|
| 1.0 | [Date] | [Name] | Initial SOP created |
| 1.1 | [Date] | [Name] | [Update details] |

tips: Write each step in active voice so the reader knows exactly what action to take.
Test the SOP with someone who has never completed the task before.
Include a clear Definition of Done so quality expectations are obvious.
Store SOPs in a central knowledge base where team members can find them quickly.

faqs.question: What is a standard operating procedure?
faqs.answer: A standard operating procedure is a documented set of instructions that explains how to complete a recurring task or process consistently.

faqs.question: What should an SOP include?
faqs.answer: An SOP should include the title, purpose, scope, roles, required resources, step-by-step procedure, quality standards, troubleshooting guidance, document control, and approval information.

faqs.question: Who should write an SOP?
faqs.answer: An SOP should be written by someone who understands the process well, often with input from the employees, contractors, or stakeholders who perform or review the work.

faqs.question: How often should SOPs be reviewed?
faqs.answer: Most SOPs should be reviewed every six to twelve months or whenever a process, tool, regulation, or responsibility changes.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a process and an SOP?
faqs.answer: A process explains what needs to happen at a high level, while an SOP explains exactly how to complete the task step by step.

faqs.question: What format works best for an SOP?
faqs.answer: Simple tasks work well as numbered steps or checklists, while complex workflows may require hierarchical steps, screenshots, diagrams, or flowcharts.
